name: CA-30
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's +21 Democratic partisan lean in a heavily blue Los Angeles-area seat
Incumbent Laura Friedman has a large financial edge: about $469,000 on hand versus roughly $2,600 for Scott Meyers
Prediction markets price the Democratic side near 97% to win
No competitive polling or expert ratings, but no evidence of a serious challenge either
model.rationale: The fundamentals point overwhelmingly to Friedman: a +21 Democratic district, incumbency, and a lopsided fundraising advantage over a Republican challenger with almost no cash. Markets agree, pricing this near-certain for the Democrat, so the forecast stays firmly in Safe D territory.
model.watch: A surprise would require an external scandal or redistricting-level shock, since no polling or spending signals suggest the race is competitive.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Laura Friedman, a Democratic incumbent, defends a Los Angeles-area House seat with a +21 Democratic partisan lean. She won the seat in 2024 and advanced to the general election, where she faces Republican Scott Meyers. The structural conditions in this district make a Democratic victory the overwhelming expectation.

The resource gap is stark: Friedman has raised about $828,000 and holds roughly $469,000 in cash, while Meyers has raised under $60,000 with only about $2,600 available and no outside support on either side. Prediction markets price the Democratic side near 97%. With no competitive polling and no expert ratings flagging the race, everything points to a comfortable Democratic win.
